name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about six points on the partisan baseline
Salinas is an incumbent with a large financial edge ($1.6M raised vs. $13K)
No outside spending against Salinas and no public polling of the race
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances around 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Salinas: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage over David Russ, who has raised almost nothing. With no contrary polling or spending evidence, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's 6th District is a first-term Democratic-held seat that leans Democratic by about six points. Incumbent Andrea Salinas is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.6 million with over $600,000 on hand, while Republican David Russ has raised about $13,000 with almost no cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Salinas.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets put Democratic win odds around 95%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes Salinas a clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
